subject: Next steps: inference feature-gap & parity test plan
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Menon <sanjay@orbitai.com>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.k@orbitai.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: inference feature-gap & parity test plan

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the intro call earlier. Good to meet you and Priya. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and what a small PoC would look like.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary objective: validate production parity for real-time chat experience (function/tool calling + structured JSON outputs + streaming) against hyperscaler APIs you’re evaluating.
- Top acceptance criteria you called out: fidelity of function-calls (argument accuracy), JSON schema conformance for structured outputs, streaming latency under 100ms per-chunk at your expected concurrency, and predictable token costs.

Proposed quick parity plan (high level):
1) Controlled benchmark: 250 request scenarios covering toy and edge cases (50 function-calling, 50 structured-output, 100 streaming/low-latency prompts, 50 misc).
2) Metrics: end-to-end latency p50/p95, per-token latency, function-call success rate (exact match / best-effort), JSON schema validation rate, cost per 1k tokens.
3) Environments: Redwood hosted + Azure OpenAI + AWS Bedrock (or an API proxy you prefer). If you want, we can ask CloudWrangle to provision a short trial infra to mimic your production concurrency.
4) Deliverables: raw logs, benchmark scripts, short slide deck with results and a recommended config (batching/quantization/caching) for production.

Attached is a short checklist and a proposed test-matrix (parity-test-matrix.xlsx). I’ve also created a shared Drive doc for the test matrix: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cParityPlan.

Can you:
- Confirm the dataset you want us to use (sanitized chat history or synthetic prompts)?
- Confirm which hyperscalers/APIs you want in scope (Azure/AWS/Google/other)?
- Indicate target concurrency and SLOs for streaming (e.g., 50 concurrent users, 150ms chunk latency target)?

If agreeable I’ll loop in Marissa (SE) and Aditya (Sales Lead) to finalize the matrix and quote a short PoC timeline. Ideally we kickoff next week.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Sanjay Menon <sanjay@orbitai.com>

Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: inference feature-gap & parity test plan

Thanks Lauren — this looks great and matches what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Benchmark methodology: for function-calling fidelity, can you describe how you’ll measure 'argument accuracy'? E.g., strict exact-match vs. semantic match?
2) Quantization/precision: will you run tests on LLM variants (int8/qat) or only float32/float16 profiles initially? We’re sensitive to both latency and output fidelity.
3) Hyperscalers in scope: we want Azure OpenAI + AWS Bedrock for sure. We’re also trialing a smaller API (CloudWrangle) that our infra team wants to include for cost comparison — I’ll loop Ben Harper if needed.

Dataset: we’ll provide a sanitized subset of customer prompts (~2k rows) by Friday. Target concurrency we’re thinking: 80 concurrent sessions, with a 120ms chunk latency goal for streaming.

If you can share the test matrix and an initial timeline/estimates, we’ll prioritize this internally.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Menon
Head of Product, OrbitAI
Sanjay.Menon@orbitai.com

Folks — forwarding OrbitAI’s reply and the initial checklist. Key asks: they’ll provide a sanitized dataset (~2k), want Azure + AWS + CloudWrangle included, target concurrency ~80 sessions and streaming chunk latency target ~120ms.

Proposed internal action items: 
- Marissa: can you draft the concrete test harness and a short script for the function-calling fidelity tests? For fidelity, I think we should report both exact-match and a Levenshtein/semantic score for arguments. Please add any tooling/measurements you need to the matrix attachment.
- Aditya: can you confirm we’re comfortable running quantized variants? Also want your guidance on whether we should run int8 vs bf16 baseline for the first pass.
- Stephanie: heads-up that OrbitAI will likely ask for an NDA amendment (data handling / sanitized logs). Can legal prepare a short addendum?

I’ve attached the parity-test-matrix.xlsx (work-in-progress) and the one-pager. My target: propose a 2-week PoC timeline (week 1: test run + logs, week 2: analysis + recommendations).

Thanks —
Lauren

Thanks Lauren — I reviewed the matrix and sketched an initial test plan. High level notes: 

- Function-calling fidelity: we’ll run 150 calls (mix of single and multi-argument calls). Reporting: exact-match rate, normalized edit distance, and a 'semantic correctness' flag based on lightweight heuristics and sample human eval (20 examples).
- Structured outputs: use JSON schema enforcement with JSONLint + schema-aware parsing. Failure modes will be categorized (malformed JSON, missing keys, type mismatches).
- Streaming: we’ll measure chunk latency and startup latency. For streaming we’ll instrument both SDK-level and network-level latency so we can attribute where slowdowns happen.
- Environments: Redwood hosted (baseline), Redwood with int8 quantization profile, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, CloudWrangle (Ben — if you can provide a short-term non-prod endpoint/credits that would be great).

Timing & next steps:
- Monday: finalize matrix and test scripts (I’ll upload to the shared Drive docs).
- Wed/Thu: run 1st pass of tests against Redwood hosted + Azure + AWS.
- Following Mon: run CloudWrangle if Ben can provision.
- Deliverable: slide deck + raw logs + a config recommendation by end of week 2.

Notes for Aditya: I’ll need one GPU-backed runner for int8 tests and a small S3 bucket (pre-signed) for log upload. I’ll annotate cost delta per run.

Ben — looping you per Sanjay’s note. Can CloudWrangle spin up a short test endpoint or provide API credits for a week? If yes we’ll add you to the Drive doc and share the matrix.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
